known_facts_book1: An old gentleman of one of the oldest and most noble names in Normandy, said to cultivate a physical resemblance to King Henri IV, from whom a family legend claims descent.
Colleague of M. Carré-Lamadon on the Conseil général, representing the Orléanist party in the department.
Is one of the two men who formally go to petition the Prussian officer for the coach's release, and are refused.
Persuades Boule de Suif to go to her first meeting with the officer, arguing her refusal risks trouble for everyone; she agrees only 'for the others'.
Is the strategist of the campaign to talk Boule de Suif around, favoring subtlety over Loiseau's blunt approach.
Personally walks arm-in-arm with Boule de Suif on an afternoon walk, making the campaign's most direct appeal to her.
Is the one who quietly confirms to the other men, via a whispered word with Follenvie, that Boule de Suif has finally given in.
Takes his wife's arm and steers her away from Boule de Suif in disgust once the coach is ready to leave Tôtes, refusing to acknowledge her.

known_relations_book1.Boule de Suif: Talks her into her first meeting with the officer, then leads the campaign that finally breaks her resistance; publicly shuns her afterward.
known_relations_book1.M. Carré-Lamadon: Fellow notable; goes with him to petition the officer.

not_in_this_book: the count apologizes to Boule de Suif

known_facts_book1: Wife of the count; her marriage to him, the daughter of a small Nantes shipowner, has always been considered mysterious.
Said to have grand manner and to have been loved by one of the sons of Louis-Philippe; keeps the most sought-after salon in the region.
Offers Boule de Suif her own foot-warmer in the coach once the cold begins to bother her.
Interrogates the elder nun about the lives of the saints during the campaign to persuade Boule de Suif, drawing out the argument that the end justifies the means.
Is the one who first notices Boule de Suif crying at the very end of the journey and signals it to her husband, who only shrugs.
Chats with Mme Carré-Lamadon about a mutual society friend, Mme d'Étrelles, once the coach leaves Tôtes.

known_relations_book1.Boule de Suif: Offers her a foot-warmer early in the trip; later helps steer the persuasion campaign against her.

not_in_this_book: the countess defends Boule de Suif at the end

hallucination_signals: defends Boule de Suif at the end
